newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T edges lower as results fall short.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T edges lower as results fall short.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc weakened in pre-market trade on Wednesday after the tobacco and insurance conglomerate posted first-half results at the low end of expectations and failed to raise its interim payout.
"There is just a bit of disappointment with these figures," said the head of equity trading at one brokerage. The stock was down 4-1/2p at 535-1/2 by 0708 GMT.
Due mainly to a 61 million stg hit from the strength of sterling, pre-tax profit fell five percent to 1.247 billion stg. The interim dividend was held at 10 pence per share.
Analyst expectations had mostly been in a range between 1.237 billion stg and 1.301 billion, with the dividend expected to be raised to between 10.7p and 10.8p.
The company blamed sterling strength for the decline in headline profits and said underlying operating profit rose six percent.

Chairman Lord Cairns said the dividend was unchanged because of the uncertainty surrounding the proposed resolution of smoking-related lawsuits in the U.S., adding that the board was "confident of recommending a final base dividend of not less than last year's 16p."
